note: Original grammar check-in and numbered practice packs. Each item: three sentences, one correct. Correct sentences must pass the pack's errors.js detectors and, where a detector exists, the wrong sentences it names must trip it (tools/access-grammar.test.mjs). Practice, not a level.

rule.en: Use 'an' before a vowel sound and 'a' before a consonant sound. Use 'the' for one thing both people already know.
rule.es: Usa 'an' antes de un sonido de vocal y 'a' antes de un sonido de consonante. Usa 'the' para algo que las dos personas ya conocen.

choices: She ate an apple at lunch.
She ate a apple at lunch.
She ate apple an at lunch.
We waited a hour for the bus.
We waited an hour for the bus.
We waited hour for the bus.

why.en: 'Interesting' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.
why.es: 'Interesting' empieza con sonido de vocal, así que se usa 'an'.

choices: My cousin is an university student.
My cousin is university a student.
My cousin is a university student.

why.en: 'University' starts with a 'you' sound, a consonant sound, so use 'a'.
why.es: 'University' empieza con el sonido 'yu', que es de consonante, así que se usa 'a'.

choices: I saw a elephant at the zoo.
I saw an elephant at the zoo.
I saw elephant an at the zoo.

why.en: 'Elephant' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.
why.es: 'Elephant' empieza con sonido de vocal, así que se usa 'an'.

choices: Please close the door behind you.
Please close a door behind you.

why.en: Both people know which door, so use 'the'.
why.es: Las dos personas saben de qué puerta se habla, así que se usa 'the'.

choices: He wants to be a engineer.
He wants to be an engineer.

why.en: A job after 'be' needs an article, and 'engineer' starts with a vowel sound.
why.es: Una profesión después de 'be' necesita artículo, y 'engineer' empieza con sonido de vocal.

title.en: Plurals: one and more than one
title.es: Plurales: uno y más de uno

rule.en: After a number bigger than one, a countable noun takes -s or -es. Adjectives never take -s.
rule.es: Después de un número mayor que uno, un sustantivo contable lleva -s o -es. Los adjetivos nunca llevan -s.

choices: I have three book in my bag.
I have three books in my bag.
I have three bookes in my bag.
We planted two tree near the school.
We planted two trees near the school.
We planted two treees near the school.

why.en: 'Two' means more than one, so 'tree' becomes 'trees'.
why.es: 'Two' significa más de uno, así que 'tree' cambia a 'trees'.

choices: The class has five boxes of markers.
The class has five box of markers.
The class has five boxs of markers.

why.en: Nouns ending in -x add -es: box, boxes.
why.es: Los sustantivos que terminan en -x agregan -es: box, boxes.

why.en: Adjectives like 'different' stay the same with plural nouns.
why.es: Los adjetivos como 'different' no cambian con sustantivos en plural.

choices: How much students are in the club?
How many student are in the club?
How many students are in the club?

why.en: Use 'many' with nouns you can count, and the noun is plural.
why.es: Usa 'many' con sustantivos que se pueden contar, y el sustantivo va en plural.

why.en: 'Four' is more than one, so add -s: horses.
why.es: 'Four' es más de uno, así que se agrega -s: horses.

rule.en: Add 's to show that something belongs to a person: Ana's book. Use his, her, their before the thing, not after.
rule.es: Agrega 's para mostrar que algo pertenece a una persona: Ana's book. Usa his, her, their antes de la cosa, no después.

choices: The book of Maria is on the desk.
Maria's book is on the desk.
Marias book is on the desk.
The students opened the notebooks of them.
The bike of my brother is blue.

why.en: One brother owns the bike, so write brother's.
why.es: Un hermano es dueño de la bicicleta, así que se escribe brother's.

choices: She forgot she lunch at home.
She forgot her lunch at home.
She forgot the lunch of her at home.

why.en: Use 'her' before the thing a girl or woman owns.
why.es: Usa 'her' antes de lo que pertenece a una niña o mujer.

choices: The dog wagged the tail of it.

why.en: 'Its' shows belonging. 'It's' means 'it is'.
why.es: 'Its' muestra pertenencia. 'It's' significa 'it is'.

choices: The teacher's desk is by the window.
The desk of the teacher is by the window.
The teachers desk is by the window.

why.en: One teacher owns the desk: teacher's desk.
why.es: Una maestra es dueña del escritorio: teacher's desk.

choices: The team of us won the game.

why.en: Use 'our' before something that belongs to us.
why.es: Usa 'our' antes de algo que nos pertenece.

rule.en: A pronoun replaces a noun. Use he for a boy or man, she for a girl or woman, it for a thing, they for more than one. English sentences need the subject pronoun.
rule.es: Un pronombre reemplaza a un sustantivo. Usa he para un niño u hombre, she para una niña o mujer, it para una cosa, they para más de uno. Las oraciones en inglés necesitan el pronombre sujeto.

choices: My sister is tall. He plays basketball.
My sister is tall. She plays basketball.
My sister is tall. Plays basketball.
The plants need water. It are dry.
The plants need water. They are dry.
The plants need water. Are dry.

why.en: 'Plants' is more than one, so use 'they'.
why.es: 'Plants' es más de uno, así que se usa 'they'.

choices: Mr. Lee is my coach. She is kind.
Mr. Lee is my coach. It is kind.
Mr. Lee is my coach. He is kind.

why.en: 'Mr.' names a man, so use 'he'.
why.es: 'Mr.' nombra a un hombre, así que se usa 'he'.

choices: It is important to drink water.

why.en: English needs a subject. Start with 'It is'.
why.es: El inglés necesita un sujeto. Empieza con 'It is'.

choices: Me and Sam went to the library.
Sam and I went to the library.
Sam and me went to the library.

why.en: Before the verb, use 'I', and name the other person first.
why.es: Antes del verbo usa 'I', y nombra primero a la otra persona.

choices: The teacher gave the paper to her.
The teacher gave the paper to she.
The teacher gave the paper to hers.

why.en: After 'to', use 'her'.
why.es: Después de 'to', se usa 'her'.

rule.en: Use 'on' for days and dates, 'in' for months and years, and 'at' for clock times.
rule.es: Usa 'on' para días y fechas, 'in' para meses y años, y 'at' para la hora.

why.en: Use 'in' with months.
why.es: Usa 'in' con los meses.

why.en: Use 'on' with days of the week.
why.es: Usa 'on' con los días de la semana.

why.en: Use 'at' with a time of day like noon.
why.es: Usa 'at' con una hora del día como noon.

why.en: Use 'in' with years.
why.es: Usa 'in' con los años.

why.en: Use 'on' with days of the week.
why.es: Usa 'on' con los días de la semana.

rule.en: Use don't, doesn't or didn't before the base verb. Use only one negative word in one idea.
rule.es: Usa don't, doesn't o didn't antes del verbo base. Usa solo una palabra negativa en una idea.

choices: She didn't went to the park.
She didn't go to the park.
She no went to the park.

why.en: After 'didn't', use the base verb: go.
why.es: Después de 'didn't', usa el verbo base: go.

why.en: 'Don't' is already the negative, so use 'anything'.
why.es: 'Don't' ya es la negación, así que se usa 'anything'.

why.en: With he, she or it, use 'doesn't' and the base verb.
why.es: Con he, she o it, usa 'doesn't' y el verbo base.

why.en: 'Can't' is already negative, so use 'anybody'.
why.es: 'Can't' ya es negativo, así que se usa 'anybody'.

why.en: After 'didn't', use the base verb: see.
why.es: Después de 'didn't', usa el verbo base: see.

rule.en: In a question, the helping verb (do, does, did, is, are, can) comes before the subject.
rule.es: En una pregunta, el verbo auxiliar (do, does, did, is, are, can) va antes del sujeto.

choices: What time does the bus come?
What time does the bus comes?

why.en: Put 'does' before the subject and use the base verb.
why.es: Pon 'does' antes del sujeto y usa el verbo base.

why.en: 'Is' comes before the subject 'the sky'.
why.es: 'Is' va antes del sujeto 'the sky'.

why.en: After 'did', use the base verb: finish.
why.es: Después de 'did', usa el verbo base: finish.

why.en: 'Can' comes before the subject in a question.
why.es: 'Can' va antes del sujeto en una pregunta.

choices: How many pages did you read?
How many pages did you readed?

why.en: Add 'did' before 'you' and keep the base verb.
why.es: Agrega 'did' antes de 'you' y deja el verbo base.
